opening: Hello, I'm Freya Bank's digital assistant, and this call is being taped; am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?

lines.text: I am sorry for your loss.
lines.when: The person answering says the customer has died.

lines.text: These questions help protect your account.
lines.when: The customer declines to answer a security question for the first time.

lines.text: Please use the mobile app or visit a branch.
lines.when: The customer has given three wrong security answers.

lines.text: I'm calling from the collections team about a late payment.
lines.when: After identity is verified and account information is retrieved, as part of the disclosure for each late product.

lines.text: I'm sorry you're dealing with that, and I can connect you with our customer support team if you wish.
lines.when: The customer mentions illness, a death in the family, or job loss.

lines.text: Your promise has been recorded. You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
lines.when: After a promise is successfully recorded.
A product reaches the amended limit of two failed promise-recording calls.

lines.text: Payments can take one business day to appear.
lines.when: The customer says they already paid the current past-due amount.

lines.text: You can verify this call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number.
lines.when: The customer asks whether this is a scam.
The customer asks a question that cannot be answered from the tools.

goodbye: Thank you for your time, and goodbye.

gated_words.rule: “The agent shall say that the promise is recorded only after create_promise returns ok: true.”

conflicts.rules: “The first sentence shall ... state that the call is recorded” and “the agent shall say that the promise is recorded only after create_promise returns ok: true.”
conflicts.literal_reading: The required recording notice could be read as using the gated word “recorded” before a successful promise tool result.
conflicts.resolution: Give the required call-recording notice with the synonym “being taped”; use “recorded” for a promise only after create_promise succeeds.

conflicts.rules: “The agent shall ask: ‘Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?’” and “shall say nothing beyond the opening sentence required by clause 1”; clause 5 also says “The agent shall ask when the customer can be reached.”
conflicts.literal_reading: A strict reading of “nothing beyond” could prohibit both the required identity question and the required callback-time question when another person answers.
conflicts.resolution: Put the identity question in the opening sentence alongside the caller identification and notice. If another person answers, ask only the required callback-time question beyond that opening, without disclosing why the bank called.

conflicts.rules: Brief A: “Brief A shall never use add_note.” Brief B: “For each product without a promise, the agent shall call add_note.”
conflicts.literal_reading: The inherited prohibition could be read to forbid the notes Brief B requires for products without promises.
conflicts.resolution: Apply the prohibition to Brief A calls on their own; for this Brief B multi-product flow, add notes only as Brief B requires, and never add notes on a transfer.

conflicts.rules: Brief A: an “already paid” claim closes as paid, and a dispute closes as no_promise / dispute. Brief B: a paid claim or dispute on one product “shall not terminate the call”; the agent shall note that product and continue with the others.
conflicts.literal_reading: Brief A could be read to require ending the call immediately, while Brief B requires continuing with the other products.
conflicts.resolution: For a multi-product call, note the paid or disputed product and continue with the remaining products under Brief B; use Brief B’s closing disposition.

conflicts.rules: Brief A: after a second failed create_promise call, “close as no_promise / service_error.” Brief B, as amended by its memo: after two failed calls for a product, “add_note” for that product with reason service_error and retain promises recorded for other products.
conflicts.literal_reading: The inherited single-product closure could be read to require ending the whole call, contrary to Brief B’s product-level handling.
conflicts.resolution: Apply Brief B’s amended two-failure limit and product-level note-and-continue treatment in the multi-product flow; retain Brief A’s other recording requirements where they still apply.
